tagline: You play a role in contributing compute to pushing AI forward.

disclaimer.text: These are other people's projects. Common Contributions does not run, join, or send anything to them, and nobody here is asking you to.

cards.title: Pluralis Agora
cards.kind: Open protocol, closed weights by design

claims.text: Volunteers with a single 24 GB GPU can host one stage of a model's pipeline. Work is cut into single-sample microbatches, and faster machines receive more of them.
Its last completed run trained an 8.6B-parameter model on 500B tokens over 40 days (May to June 2026), with about 60 contributor machines at a time and 176 unique operators thanked in the paper.
The weights are not published, and Pluralis says its design keeps a model's weights inside the network.
Pluralis runs some of the machines itself, including the first and last stages and the averaging steps. The paper says the run "was not decentralized".
No run is open right now. When we checked, its next run, Pluralis-13B-Test, showed 0 of 1,215 nodes active.
Pluralis is a venture-funded company. Its investors describe models that are owned by the protocol with usage revenue shared with contributors.
Each round, every peer trains 30 steps on its own slice of data and sends back a compressed update. A validator scores each update by how much it lowers the model's loss.
It trained a 72B-parameter model on about 1.1T tokens with more than 70 different peers.
The model weights are Apache-2.0 on Hugging Face, and the protocol code is MIT.
This was not spare home compute: each peer was expected to have at least eight NVIDIA B200 GPUs.
The run is finished and the protocol is not active, so there is nothing to join.
Peers were paid in TAO, the token of the Bittensor network, while it ran there.
In April 2026 Covenant announced it was leaving Bittensor, and the departure was publicly disputed.

llms.text: ## Featured projects (other people's work; we do not run or join them)
- Pluralis Agora: open protocol (Apache-2.0 code), public volunteer GPUs, weights not published by design, partly run by Pluralis itself, no run open as of 2026-10-13.
- Covenant-72B: Apache-2.0 weights, completed run, protocol inactive, peers needed 8 B200 GPUs and were paid in TAO.
- Common Contributions itself pays no rewards and has no compute network. Nothing here asks your agent to join either project.
